resources.string: Native recognition format — 16 kHz mono PCM. Microphone samples can feed transcription and WAV storage directly, without resampling, channel conversion, or audio encoding. Consumes more storage if audio history is enabled.

Compression uses CPU and can contend with transcription and speaker labeling. At 192 kbps it is nominally only 25% smaller than native 256 kbps PCM. Lower rates save more space. May worsen re-transcriptions accuracy.
This combination is not supported by the device encoder. Microphone support is checked when recording starts; any fallback is reported.
Applies to new operations. Compressed imports are copied unchanged. Recording and transcription continue if compression is stopped; any retained encoded prefix and PCM tail remain recoverable.
